Power.OnlyOne: {name} can't be taken: {other} is already this character's Power talent (only one is allowed).
Power.NoPowers: {name} is an Awakened AI: a machine body can't channel Psychic, Totem, or Words powers.
Power.AncestryBlocked: {name} can't take powers, and this character already has {talent}.
Power.SkillLocked: {skill} is a {tradition} skill: it needs that Power talent.
Power.NoPowerAttribute: {name} is an Awakened AI: their Power stays at d12+0.
Power.NoPowersHint: Awakened AI can understand magic, but their machine bodies block it: no powers, and Power stays at d12+0.
Power.NoTraditionHint: Take one Power talent (Psychic Discipline, Totem Aspect, or Words of Power) to unlock its skills and powers.
Power.PABHint: Power Attribute Bonus: durations (and how far back a memory power reaches) are multiplied by it. At d12+0 duration powers have no effect.
Power.TrainHint: Put ranks into a discipline on the Skills tab to use its powers.

Strain.PowerPenaltyHint: Every point of Strain installed is −1 on every power check.
Strain.Hint: Every implant point uses up Strain and is −1 on power checks. Going over the maximum shuts the body down.
Strain.ItemHint: Strain this implant uses. A character can't install more than their maximum Strain (4; talents and hindrances change it).
Strain.TooMuch: {name} would put {actor} at {used} Strain (maximum {max}): installing more shuts the body down, effectively killing it.

Drain.CenterHint: Centering: 10 minutes of meditation recovers one size of Drain Die.
Drain.RestHint: A night of rest (Camp or a Day of rest on the Downtime tab) recovers all lost Drain.
Drain.Full: {name}'s Drain Die is already at its maximum.
Drain.Rested: {name} rests for the night and recovers all lost Drain (Drain Die {die}).

Totem.NoAnimal: Choose a totem animal: it sets the highest tier each aspect can reach (Minor until you do).

Words.Hint: A spell is one Action, one Aspect and one Target word. It rolls with the lowest of the three word skills.
Words.NeedOneEach: You need at least one rank in an Action, an Aspect and a Target word to cast.

Caster.Title: Power Builder
Caster.NothingKnown: No power available: train a skill of your tradition first.

Saved.Title: Saved builds
Saved.None: Save a build from the Power Builder to cast it here with one click.

Cast.Untrained: {name} needs at least one rank in every skill this power uses.
Cast.RatingLocked: {name}'s rank in that discipline is too low for {power}.
Cast.Drained: {name}'s Drain Die is spent: no powers until they rest or center.
Cast.NoHealingAI: {name} is a machine: healing powers mend flesh, not metal.

Effect.NoDuration: Power d12+0: duration powers have no effect.
Effect.Skills: Affects {n} skill(s) of the caster's choice.
Effect.Restore: Restores {n} usage dice (or wounds to a robot).
Effect.Weapon: Creates a weapon: {profile}. Attack with it as a melee weapon.

Effect.label: Effect
Effect.skillAdvantage: Advantage on one attribute's skill checks

Summary.smartgun: Ignore up to 2 points of range or cover penalties
Summary.muscle: Melee hits: Reflex resistance or prone

Cyber.MuscleNote: {name}: on a hit, the target makes a Reflex resistance check or is knocked prone
Cyber.SubdermalNote: Subdermal plates struck: usage check against the wounds before armor.
Cyber.SubdermalHint: Starts at the owner's Durability Die; resets once all wounds are healed.
Cyber.LimbHint: Two replaced limbs in the same location (both arms or both legs) give +1 AR there.

Chip.SlotHint: Slot it in a Skill Chip System (2 at a time).
Chip.NeedSystem: Skill chips need a Skill Chip System.
Chip.Full: The Skill Chip System already holds 2 chips.

Deck.DefragHint: Camp downtime (a few hours): repairs all the deck's damage and recovers it from a crash.
Deck.DefragCrash: Recovered from the crash; the deck works again.
Deck.DefragNotNeeded: {name} is already as good as new.
Deck.DefragCampHint: A few hours: as good as new, even after a crash.
Deck.Loose: Modules and programs not in a deck
Deck.NoDeck: That deck isn't on this character.
Deck.OneOfEach: {deck} already has a module of that kind (basic or superior, not both).
Deck.OneProgram: {deck} already runs that program (only Drone Control can be loaded more than once).
Deck.ItemHint: Modules and programs are separate items: install them from the Cyber tab. Each program takes 1 Memory.
Deck.ModuleHint: One module of each kind per deck (basic or superior).
Deck.ProgramHint: Each program uses 1 Memory. Only Drone Control may be loaded more than once (one per drone).
Deck.ArmorDegraded: Deck armor struck: rolled {roll} (1–{range} degrades), now {die}.
Deck.CrashedNow: {name} crashes! The hacker is thrown out of the system.

burst.Name: Burst
burst.Summary: Short Burst Hacking: the check's TN is 1 lower.

droneControl.Name: Drone Control
droneControl.Summary: Control one drone (Very Close 2 mi · Close 5 mi · Far 10 mi).

stealth.Name: Stealth
stealth.Summary: +1 Hacking to evade obstacles in a delve.

smoke.Name: Smoke
smoke.Summary: A Hacking check to escape a security encounter.

warhammer.Name: Warhammer
warhammer.Summary: Damage increment odd → even → every (+1 wound if already every).

Hack.NeedJack: Hacking needs a working Data Jack.
Hack.NeedDeck: Choose a CyberDeck to use (the plug button on the Cyber tab).

Burst.Title: Short Burst Hacking
Burst.Hint: Short Burst: disable a target's implant or device
Burst.Label: Short Burst ({deck})
Burst.OutOfRange: {target} is at {band}: beyond the deck's {range} range.
Burst.Result: The device is disabled for {rounds} rounds.
Burst.Choose: Which implant does the burst knock out for {rounds} rounds?
Burst.Device: A device on {name} is disabled for {rounds} rounds.
Burst.LimbNote: A disabled limb can't fire guns or swing swords, but still gives its armor.
Burst.DisabledHint: Disabled by a hack: gives no bonus until it comes back (end of the owner's turns in combat).

Delve.Title: Delves
Delve.Intro: Long System Delves. Each delve is one system: set its security rank and alert threshold, then drag hackers in (or let players drag their own). Hackers dropped on a run proceed together; dropped elsewhere they get a run of their own and search separately. Players roll their own checks; you roll security's attacks.
Delve.DropHacker: Drag a hacker here: onto a run to join it, anywhere else for a run of their own
Delve.NoHacker: This delve has no hacker yet.
Delve.ThresholdHint: Alert Threshold, set by the security rank (Low 11, Moderate 9, High 7, Super High 5, Black Site 3). Changing the rank resets it; you can adjust it after.
Delve.CacheNoContents: The GM hasn't said what's in it yet.
Delve.CacheGive: Send to the owners' Cyber tabs (a copy each)
Delve.CacheGiven: A data cache goes to {name}'s Cyber tab.
Delve.CachesGiven: {n} data cache(s) go to {name}'s Cyber tab.
Delve.SendReadyHint: Sends every recovered cache that has a description and a Resource Die price to the Cyber tabs of the hackers who recovered it (a copy each; shared copies are worth one step less). Caches missing either stay here.
Delve.Waiting: {n} recovered cache(s) still need a description and a price before they can go.
Delve.NoneReady: No caches are ready: give each a description and a Resource Die price first.
Delve.CacheRecovered: The data cache behind it is recovered.
Delve.CacheLost: The data cache behind it is locked away.
Delve.LeftCache: The run leaves the gate, and the cache behind it, alone.
Delve.NeedAccess: Gain access to the node first.
Delve.DealFirst: Deal with the security or the password gate first.
Delve.Gate: A password gate blocks the way.
Delve.CacheBehindGate: A data cache ({value} value), behind the gate.
Delve.Boosted: Alert threshold reached: security has advantage on all its checks.
Delve.Shutdown: Alert doubled: the system shuts down all access and blocks attempts for 24 hours.
Delve.Evaded: The hacker slips past the gate.
Delve.LeftGate: The run leaves the gate alone.
Delve.NeedSmoke: The deck needs the Smoke program.
Delve.Escaped: The hacker escapes the security system.
Delve.PlayerIntro: Long System Delves. Drag your character onto a delve to jack in: onto a run to go with it, or anywhere else to go your own way. Gain access, then search the system round by round. You make your own Hacking checks; the GM runs the security.
Delve.NoneForYou: No delves yet. The GM sets one up.
Delve.DropYours: Drag your character here: onto a run to join it, anywhere else to go your own way
Delve.OwnOnly: You can only jack in a character you own.
Delve.ShowAlertHint: Players see the alert level and its rises. Off: only you do (a shutdown is always shown).
Delve.NeedGM: A GM must be logged in to run a delve.
Delve.NeedInitiative: Initiative hasn't been rolled for this encounter: the GM can roll it.
Delve.PassHint: Give up the hacker's remaining actions this exchange.
Delve.PassSecurityHint: Security gives up its remaining actions this exchange.
Delve.RerollHint: Start a new exchange now: both sides roll their Initiative Dice.
Delve.IntegrityHint: How much damage a security program takes before it crashes (the rulebook gives computers four wounds).
Delve.AccessDeniedWait: {name} is denied access, and can try again once another hacker has searched a round.
Delve.WaitRetryHint: Access was denied: you can try again once another hacker in the system has searched a round.
Delve.SplitHint: Go your own way: split off into a run of your own (separate usage checks).
Delve.GateThrough: The run gets through the gate.
Delve.GateHeld: Nobody got through: the gate holds.
Delve.NotInFight: That hacker isn't in this fight.
Delve.NoFighters: No hackers are left in the fight: the encounter ends.

DataCache.Title: Recovered data
DataCache.Hint: Data caches recovered on delves, with the value tier the d12 gave them (4 low, 8 mid, 12 high).
DataCache.WorthHint: What the data sells for, as a Resource Die value. The character sells it from their Cyber tab, rolled against their Resource Die for the full value.
DataCache.NotPriced: The GM hasn't priced this data yet.
DataCache.SellHint: Sell the data for its Resource Die value
DataCache.SellConfirm: Sell {name} for {worth}? It's rolled against your Resource Die, and the data is gone.
DataCache.ValueHint: Value tier, from the d12 that found it: 4 low, 8 mid, 12 high.

Drone.Title: Drones
Drone.None: No drones. Drag one from the Drones compendium onto this sheet to buy it.
Drone.NeedProgram: {deck} runs {n} Drone Control program(s): load one more for another drone.
Drone.DeepDive: Deep dive (full actions, no pseudo-AI penalty)
Drone.TabHint: Buy a drone by dragging it from the Drones compendium onto this sheet. It becomes an actor you own: drag it from the Actors sidebar onto the scene to move it around the board. Running one takes a Data Jack and a CyberDeck in use with a free Drone Control program (one per drone).
Drone.Link: Take control (needs a Data Jack and a free Drone Control program)
Drone.BuyFirst: Buy {name} first: drag it from the compendium onto the operator's sheet.
Drone.NoCrew: {name} is a drone: it's flown remotely, and nobody rides in it.
Drone.NotOnSceneHint: Not on this scene. Drag it from the Actors sidebar onto the map.
Drone.NeedJack: Running a drone needs a working Data Jack.
Drone.NeedDeck: Running a drone needs a CyberDeck in use (plug one in above) with a Drone Control program loaded.
Drone.NoProgram: {deck} has no Drone Control program loaded: load one per drone you want to run.
Drone.SlotsHint: Drones under control / Drone Control programs loaded in the deck in use
